A phone hotspot is likely, and the main site is unreachable. The hotspot provider’s proxy, Private DNS, VPN, carrier, or forwarding path may be responsible.
Suggestion: disable the hotspot provider’s VPN/proxy/Private DNS, or compare with another Wi‑Fi/mobile network.
No usable network connection is available.
Suggestion: connect to Wi‑Fi or mobile data and run diagnostics again.
Network & hotspot environment
A VPN is active, but the main site is still unreachable. The VPN exit may be rejected by Cloudflare, the node route may be faulty, or the protocol may be interfered with.
Suggestion: switch VPN nodes or protocols, or temporarily disable the VPN for comparison.
A network connection exists, but Android has not validated internet access. A hotspot login page, captive portal, Private DNS, or upstream network issue may be present.
Suggestion: confirm internet access in a browser and check the hotspot portal, Private DNS, and upstream network.
Built-in Hosts IPs accept TCP connections, but the main site HTTPS request still fails. DNS is bypassed, so the problem is TLS/SNI, Cloudflare routing, or an intermediary network block.
DoH resolved the domain, but the main site HTTPS request still fails. DNS is not the problem; TLS/SNI or the route is being blocked.
Suggestion: changing domains or Hosts usually will not help; switch networks, disable an intermediary proxy, or use a working proxy.
The main site returned HTTP %1$d, and the request was rejected by the server or Cloudflare. This may be rate limiting, a regional restriction, or a risky exit IP rather than a DNS/TLS failure.
Suggestion: wait a few minutes, switch networks, or try another working proxy node.
The main site returned HTTP %1$d; the server or Cloudflare is currently having problems.
Suggestion: retry later and check the site service status.
The main site returned HTTP %1$d. The server was reached, but its home-page response is abnormal.
